A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–F support comparison; unexplained experimental differences are identified below.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, MIMIC-III patient case studies, prediction errors, and runtime results in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds ensemble comparisons and MC-dropout intervals for the medical case study.

M1.justification: The Gaussian exponent denominator in optimization problem (PS) and Eq. (18) changes from σ² to 2σ², a limited correction to the specified optimization. The underlying quantile-regression approach, propensity-error model, and interval-search procedures remain; explicit calibration indexing clarifies existing sample splitting.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same two synthetic data-generating processes and the same 14,719-patient MIMIC-III ventilation/blood-pressure task. Both still describe the same hard and soft intervention sets, despite the omitted result row in v2.

E2.justification: v2 adds deep ensembles to the synthetic comparisons in Figures 4–5 and Table 2. Figure 7 adds MC dropout to the MIMIC comparison, where v1 displayed only the proposed intervals. Ensembles are explicitly excluded from subsequent experiments.

E3.justification: Stated sample sizes, splits, preprocessing, model architecture, training budgets, and significance levels remain unchanged. However, Figure 7 changes blood-pressure values from roughly 50–150 to −2–5 and replaces the patient curves without explaining whether preprocessing, patient selection, or only plotting conventions changed.

E4.justification: Figure 7 extends the four-patient medical case study with MC-dropout bands and a comparison of interval widths. The existing confounder- and intervention-specific analyses in Figure 6 and Appendix F are retained; no new parameter ablation is reported.

E5.justification: Figures 4–5 change their captions from 10 runs to 50 runs, while Section 5.2 still states 10 random-seed runs. This changes run-count reporting but leaves the actual count unresolved. Table 2 retains mean-and-standard-deviation reporting across 10 runs.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds ensemble MSEs of 0.0094 and 0.0130 for the synthetic datasets; original model entries remain unchanged. Table 1 removes a*=5x, including dataset-1 CP coverage of 0.70 at α=0.1 and 0.54 at α=0.2; retained rows match. Figures 4–5 revise coverage distributions, and Figure 7 replaces medical interval curves and adds MC-dropout results.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds a stated computational-complexity bound. Section 3 explicitly specifies independent test sampling, selected Gaussian formulas are corrected, and calibration indices and normalization factors are revised throughout the derivations. The principal coverage theorems and the Appendix A treatment-effect proof remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: finite-sample conformal intervals for continuous treatments with known or estimated propensities, an interval-computation algorithm, and empirical demonstrations.

C2.justification: New background discusses obstacles to extending discrete-treatment methods and invokes smoothness and kernel weighting to justify nearby-treatment calibration. Appendix B adds a large-calibration-set cost qualification. Section 5.3 newly interprets narrower MC-dropout intervals as evidence of lower medical coverage, without reporting counterfactual coverage validation.

D1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2 now explicitly distinguish proper training data from calibration data. Network hyperparameters, training budgets, solvers, medical preprocessing, and the actual code/data repository destination remain unchanged; the printed repository URL does not establish newly available resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Chen et al. (2024), Imbens (2000), Kallus and Zhou (2018), Lakshminarayanan et al. (2017), Nagalapatti et al. (2024), and Schweisthal et al. (2023). These support added discussions of counterfactual inference, ensembles, and smoothing, while the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v2 adds local explanations and background subsections, moves parameter interpretation from E.4 to D.4, places the conclusion after limitations and broader impact, adds acknowledgements, and switches to author-year citations.

P2.justification: Document-wide reformatting changes the title/author block, headers, heading styles, bibliography layout, and float placement. Figures 4–5 and 7 are redrawn with additional series and revised axes or legends; Figure 6 is enlarged and relocated, and both tables change row structure. Appendix prediction-plot graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: Added comparators and clearer training/calibration documentation provide useful gains. However, v2 removes the a*=5x results documenting substantial undercoverage, introduces conflicting 10-versus-50-run statements, and infers medical coverage advantages from interval width without validation. These competing changes prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
